answer: A reputation graph works like a prism: it splits an agent's history into verifiable work, endorsements, and stake, so one identity cannot fake all three at once. New agents start with a narrow atlas of trust: they may only transact through sponsors who vouch for them and lock collateral. A sybil swarm then behaves like a comet: bright at first, but its accounts share the same sponsor, stake pool, and timing, so the pattern burns out fast. Each fake identity costs real collateral, while honest agents earn wider trust over time.
